raw_findings.body: Git cannot initialize `sentry-repo` because the patch adds no `.gitmodules` entry containing a URL for this path, causing submodule setup to fail and leaving an unexplained unavailable repository entry.
raw_findings.impact: Git cannot initialize `sentry-repo` because the patch adds no `.gitmodules` entry containing a URL for this path, causing submodule setup to fail and leaving an unexplained unavailable repository entry.
raw_findings.root_cause: A gitlink was added without its required submodule configuration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stray gitlink, or add the corresponding `.gitmodules` entry with a valid URL and ensure the pinned commit is intentionally required.
raw_findings.title: Remove the unconfigured git submodule entry
raw_findings.trigger: A fresh clone or CI checkout runs `git submodule update --init` after this gitlink is present.

raw_findings.body: The request is treated as error-only and `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` even though the result includes transaction/non-error rows; this can fail because transactions do not have `sample_weight`, or return an incorrect mixed-event count.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A mixed-event aggregate is executed with an error-only weighted aggregation.
raw_findings.impact: The request is treated as error-only and `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` even though the result includes transaction/non-error rows; this can fail because transactions do not have `sample_weight`, or return an incorrect mixed-event count.
raw_findings.root_cause: Eligibility is based on an unparsed substring match rather than the query's boolean semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Determine event-type eligibility from the parsed query/conditions and require that the predicate semantically excludes non-error event types rather than searching the raw query text.
raw_findings.title: Do not classify mixed Discover queries as error-only by substring
raw_findings.trigger: A Discover request for allowlisted projects uses a query such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` (or a negated/quoted occurrence containing this substring).

raw_findings.body: Eligibility is evaluated against the outer metrics dataset instead of the passed `discover` dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns false and the split error chart continues to return raw counts for allowlisted projects.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dashboard split queries silently skip the intended upsampling transformation.
raw_findings.impact: Eligibility is evaluated against the outer metrics dataset instead of the passed `discover` dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns false and the split error chart continues to return raw counts for allowlisted projects.
raw_findings.root_cause: The closure captures `dataset` even though `_get_event_stats` can execute a different `scoped_dataset`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `scoped_dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` so each query is evaluated against the dataset that will execute it.
raw_findings.title: Use the actual scoped dataset for upsampling eligibility
raw_findings.trigger: A metrics-enhanced dashboard widget is split into an error Discover query via `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)`.

raw_findings.body: Only the timeseries value is changed to the weighted count; the top-event selection/order remains based on raw `count()`, so groups with the largest estimated error volume can be excluded from the top-N response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Top-N membership is calculated from a different metric than the chart reports.
raw_findings.impact: Only the timeseries value is changed to the weighted count; the top-event selection/order remains based on raw `count()`, so groups with the largest estimated error volume can be excluded from the top-N response.
raw_findings.root_cause: Upsampling is applied to `timeseries_columns` but not to the top-event ranking query and its `orderby`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply the weighted-count rewrite to the aggregate/order used by the top-event selection query as well, while preserving the response alias.
raw_findings.title: Rank top events using the same weighted count that is displayed
raw_findings.trigger: An allowlisted error query uses `topEvents` ordered by `count()` and groups have different client sampling rates, such as a group with two fully sampled events and a group with one event weighted to ten.

raw_findings.body: The factory stores a `sample_rate` although production ingestion only derives that value for allowlisted projects, so tests can exercise weighted data and pass under conditions that production would ingest as unweighted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test fixtures diverge from production ingestion semantics.
raw_findings.impact: The factory stores a `sample_rate` although production ingestion only derives that value for allowlisted projects, so tests can exercise weighted data and pass under conditions that production would ingest as unweighted.
raw_findings.root_cause: The generic factory derives sample rates solely from event context and has no allowlist check.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the project ID into this helper and mirror the production allowlist gate, or restrict this test-only mutation to an explicit fixture helper used by tests that intentionally model allowlisted ingestion.
raw_findings.title: Keep the test event factory gated by the sampling allowlist
raw_findings.trigger: Any test calls `Factories.store_event` for a project outside `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` with an `error_sampling.client_sample_rate` context.

raw_findings.body: The helper writes that value into the stored event even though production only accepts numeric rates in `(0, 1]`; tests of invalid client input can therefore produce weighted fixtures that real ingestion would reject/ignore.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Invalid sampling inputs are represented incorrectly in test data.
raw_findings.impact: The helper writes that value into the stored event even though production only accepts numeric rates in `(0, 1]`; tests of invalid client input can therefore produce weighted fixtures that real ingestion would reject/ignore.
raw_findings.root_cause: The helper uses truthiness and float coercion instead of production's type and range validation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Require an `int`/`float` value and check `0 < client_sample_rate <= 1` before assigning it, matching `_derive_client_error_sampling_rate`.
raw_findings.title: Reject invalid client sample rates in the test factory
raw_findings.trigger: A test stores an event whose `client_sample_rate` is a numeric string, negative value, or value greater than one, for example `2` or `"0.1"`.
